nodes.content: Develop robotic active perception that resolves grasp-relevant occlusions while accounting for uncertain object motion induced by sensing actions.
requirements: Reduce failed grasps by 20% relative to a fixed-view baseline under matched action budgets.
Maintain object-damage rates below 1% across previously unseen object dynamics and occlusion patterns.

nodes.content: Use belief-space MPC with online action-induced motion estimates to choose grasp-informative views and probes under a 0.5% predicted-damage cap.
How can probe-induced motion uncertainty be calibrated for unseen objects when occlusion conceals their contact geometry?
Visible post-probe displacement enables conformal motion bounds with ≥95% coverage on unseen objects despite hidden contact geometry.
Collect low-force probe trajectories, calibrate displacement-conditioned motion bounds by occlusion severity, then test 95% coverage on unseen dynamics.
Run OccluProbe-200: calibrate displacement-conditioned conformal motion bounds on 150 objects; test 95% coverage across 50 unseen dynamics and occlusions.
On OccluProbe-200, displacement-conditioned bounds covered 96.2% of 1,000 motions across 50 unseen objects; each occlusion stratum exceeded 95%.
Integrate displacement-conditioned conformal bounds into belief-space MPC, since OccluProbe-200 exceeded 95% coverage in every occlusion stratum.
Benchmark conformal-bound MPC versus fixed-view grasping across 100 unseen dynamics–occlusion combinations with matched action budgets, measuring grasp failures and damage.
OccluGrasp-100 evaluation report documents paired MPC/fixed-view trials across 100 unseen combinations, matched budgets, grasp-failure reduction, and damage rates.
Fusing low-force wrist-force transients with visible displacement yields ≥95% unseen-object coverage and 20% narrower motion bounds than displacement-only calibration.
Calibrate wrist-force/displacement bounds on 150 OccluProbe-200 objects; test ≥95% coverage and ≥20% median-width reduction versus displacement-only on 50 held-out.
On OccluProbe-200, force-fused bounds narrowed median width 23% but covered only 92.8% of held-out motions, below the 95% target.
Retain displacement-only bounds: their 96.2% coverage meets calibration target, while force fusion drops coverage to 92.8% despite narrower bounds.
How should belief-space MPC reject informative probes whose worst-case induced motion could damage fragile objects under unseen dynamics?
Use occlusion-aware wrist-camera view planning with probabilistic arm-clearance constraints to avoid contact-induced motion while revealing grasp surfaces.
Calibrate force-aware damage bounds, reject probes above 0.5% predicted damage, and select clearance-constrained noncontact wrist-camera views.
Using OccluGrasp-100’s paired-trial protocol, test 0.5%-damage probe vetoes and noncontact views across 100 combinations; record failures and damage.
OccluGrasp-100 safety appendix records per-condition probe vetoes, wrist-camera clearances, paired grasp failures, and observed damage rates.
Recompute paired failure and damage rates from OccluGrasp-100 logs; audit report and safety appendix for budget parity and damage annotations.
OccluGrasp-100 audit: matched-budget failures were 30% fixed-view, 22% probe-MPC, and 23% noncontact-view MPC; damage was 1.4% and 0.6%, respectively.
Does noncontact-view MPC maintain <1% damage and ≥20% failure reduction on heavily occluded, fragile objects with unseen dynamics?
On heavily occluded, fragile unseen objects, noncontact-view MPC reduces fixed-view failures ≥20% at matched budgets while keeping damage <1%.
Power matched-budget fragile-object trials from audited 30%-versus-23% failure rates; measure noncontact-view failures and damage under severe occlusion and unseen dynamics.
Across 500 severely occluded fragile-object trials with unseen dynamics, noncontact views cut failures 31%→23% (25.8%) under matched budgets; damage: 0.6%.
Audit OccluGrasp-100 and fragile-object trial logs for stratified failure reduction, damage confidence bounds, and matched-budget compliance.
Stratified audit found translucent fragile objects had 2% damage (2/100) and only 13.3% failure reduction (30%→26%).
Continue noncontact-view MPC development, but block translucent-object deployment: aggregate targets passed, while that stratum missed both thresholds.
Polarization-assisted views with 15-mm clearance will reduce translucent-fragile grasp failures from 30% to ≤24% and damage from 2% to <1%.
Enforce the translucent-deployment block before testing polarized 15-mm-clearance views against n21’s audited 30% failure baseline and measuring damage.
In 500 translucent-fragile trials, polarized 15-mm-clearance views achieved 23% failures versus 30% fixed-view and 0.4% damage.
Under n28’s deployment block, independently replicate n31’s polarized views on 2,000 unseen translucent-fragile trials against n21’s matched-budget baseline, recording damage.
Independent 2,000-trial replication found 25% failures versus 30% fixed-view and 1.2% damage, missing both revised thresholds.
Keep translucent-object deployment blocked: pilot gains did not replicate; independent trials missed both the 20% failure-reduction and <1% damage targets.
Use 60-mm stand-off stereo-polarimetric views with conformal motion-and-clearance bounds to reveal translucent grasp surfaces without close-range contact.
Can 60-mm stand-off stereo-polarimetric views recover graspable edges through severe occlusion without underestimating clearance uncertainty on translucent objects?
At 60-mm stand-off, stereo-polarimetric views recover ≥90% occluded grasp edges, ensure ≥95% clearance coverage, and meet both goal thresholds.
Keep deployment blocked; calibrate 60-mm stereo-polarimetric clearance bounds, then test ≥90% occluded-edge recall and ≥95% coverage on unseen translucent objects.
Stratify matched-budget 60-mm stereo-polarimetric trials using polarized-view pilot and replication logs; assess edge recall, clearance coverage, failures, and damage.
Across 2,000 matched-budget unseen translucent trials, 60-mm stereo-polarimetric views achieved 91% occluded-edge recall, 96% clearance coverage, 30%→23% failures, 0.5% damage.
Using OccluGrasp-100’s fixed-view baseline, independently replicate 60-mm stereo-polarimetric trials across unseen translucent occlusions and dynamics; measure recall, clearance, failures, damage.
Independent 2,000-trial replication achieved 92% edge recall, 95.5% clearance coverage, 30%→23% failures, and 0.6% damage on unseen translucent objects.
Lift the translucent-object block only for 60-mm stereo-polarimetric MPC; independent trials reproduced failure, damage, recall, and clearance targets.
Run gated stereo-polarimetric MPC with safety-appendix clearance checks; audit matched-budget failures and damage across unseen dynamics and occlusions.
OccluGrasp-100 safety appendix v2 adds 60-mm stereo-polarimetric gating, clearance checks, and matched-budget failure and damage audits.
Use low-pressure air puffs to displace occluders, with conformal motion bounds and damage-risk vetoes selecting safe grasp-revealing actions.
Calibrate conformal air-puff motion and damage bounds; veto puffs exceeding 0.5% predicted damage, otherwise select informative puffs.
Collect 10,000 low-pressure air-puff trajectories; calibrate conformal motion bounds and test 0.5%-damage vetoes on held-out dynamics.
PuffMotion-10K contains 10,000 air-puff trajectories, held-out dynamics splits, calibrated motion bounds, and damage-veto evaluation logs.
Audit PuffMotion-10K vetoes; compare puff-MPC, appendix-v2 stereo, and fixed-view across unseen dynamics/occlusions for matched-budget grasp failures and damage.
On unseen dynamics, matched-budget fixed-view/puff/stereo failures were 30%/26%/23%; puff damage reached 1.6% versus stereo’s 0.6%, despite vetoes.
Trace puff-MPC’s 1.6% damage through PuffMotion-10K calibration residuals; prospectively test stricter vetoes for matched-budget failures and damage.
In 1,000 held-out trials, PuffMotion-10K residual-guided vetoes yielded 24% failures versus 30% fixed-view and 0.8% damage.
Do residual-guided puff vetoes maintain <1% damage and ≥20% failure reduction in unseen lightweight-object and severe-occlusion strata?
Residual-guided puff vetoes keep damage <1% and reduce fixed-view failures ≥20% within each unseen lightweight-object and severe-occlusion stratum.
Independently test residual-guided puff vetoes in 2,000 unseen lightweight-object and severe-occlusion trials, measuring matched-budget failures and damage versus fixed-view.
In 2,000 matched-budget unseen trials, lightweight failures fell 30%→23% (0.6% damage); severe-occlusion failures fell 35%→27% (0.8% damage).
Retire original puff policy (1.6% damage); conditionally permit residual-guided vetoes in tested strata after independent trials met both thresholds.
Route lightweight or severely occluded objects to 60-mm stereo views unless residual-calibrated puff damage risk stays below 0.3%.
Within n58’s permitted strata, calibrate the 0.3% puff-risk gate and compare routed versus puff-only failures and damage.
Within permitted strata, implement appendix-v2 stereo fallback and PuffMotion-10K’s 0.3% puff-risk gate; compare matched-budget grasp failures and damage.
OccluGrasp-100 safety appendix v3 adds a calibrated 0.3% puff-risk gate, stereo fallback, permitted-stratum rules, and matched-budget audit fields.
Test appendix-v3 routing against original and residual-veto puff policies across 2,000 matched-budget lightweight/severe-occlusion trials; record failures and damage.
Across 2,000 matched-budget trials, routed failures were 24% versus 32.5% fixed-view; damage was 0.5% versus residual-puff’s 0.8%.
Adopt appendix-v3 routing only in n58’s tested strata: 24% versus 32.5% failures and 0.5% damage meet both targets.
Monitor adopted appendix-v3 routing in approved strata across unseen dynamics and occlusions for matched-budget grasp failures and damage.
Appendix-v3 monitoring dashboard tracks approved-stratum matched-budget failure reduction, damage rate, puff-gate decisions, and stereo fallbacks by unseen condition.
